3. After performing investigation police submitted charge sheet being No.44 dated 30.08.2000 against the convict-appellant and others under Sections 302/34/114 of the Penal Code. Thereafter being ready, the case was transferred to the Court of Sessions and was registered ors Sessions Case No.49 of 2002 and the Court of Sessions took cognizance against the convict-appellant along with other accuse per-sons   under Sections 302/34/114 of the Penal Code. 

 4. Subsequently, the case was transferred to the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Magura for trial and disposal of the same and the said Court framed charges against the accused persons on 1106.2002 tinder Sections 302/31/114 of the Penal Code and the said charge was read over to the accused persons, who pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried in open Court. 

 6. On completion of trial of the case, the trial Court by the judgment and order dated 24.08.2009 convicted accused Shamim, A. Salam and Md. Kamal under Section 302 of the Penal Code and sentenced each of them to death and to pay fine of Tk 1,00000.00 while convicted some other accused persons under Sections 302/34/114 of the Penal Code and sentenced each of them to imprison-ment for life and to pay fine of M.1,00000.00, in default cit fine, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more. 

 9. Mr. Sarwar Ahmed, the learned senior Advocate, appearing for the convict-appellant took us through the FIR, the inquest report, the postmortem report, the charge sheet, testimonies of the witnesses, the judgments and orders passed by the trial Court and the High Court Division, connected materials on record and submit-ted that the High Court Division tailed to consider that the judgment and order of conviction is bad in law as well as in facts and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside. He next submitted that the High Court Division failed to consider that the judgment and order of conviction is based on surmise and conjecture and not on legal evidence and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside. He submitted further that the conviction and sentence of death of the convict-appellant is based on misreading and non-reading of the evidence and the High Court Division committed illegality in passing the impugned judgment as it failed to consider that the judgment and order of conviction has been passed by the trial court without applying its judicial mind as the case was not proved by the prosecution witnesses beyond reasonablel doubt and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside. He next submitted that all the prosecution witnesses are interested witness no neutral witness supported the prosecution case and as such the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside. The learned senior Counsel contended next that the prosecution witnesses did not support the 'prosecution case and both the Courts below most illegally laid emphasis on the so-called oral dying declaration of the victim. The learned senior Counsel argued next that the vital Alamats of the case had not been seized by the investigation officer. The learned senior Counsel finally submitted that the High Court Division wrongly observed that only accused Md. Shamim inflicted the knife blows on the deceased and as such the impugned judgment and order of conviction is liable to he set aside. 

 27. P.W.9, Dr. M. Shamsul Hasan, stated in his deposition that he performed the post mortem of the victim Iltutmish under a case recorded as Unnatural Death Case No.114/2000 dated 26.05.2000 by forming a medical board consisting of three doctors.  30. PW. 10. S.I Md. Abul Kashem Khandker, in his deposition stated that on 27.05.2000 while he was working as S.I. under Shalika Police Station of District- Magura the Officer-in-Charge after recording FIR of the case handed over the case record to him for investigation. He visited the place of occurrence, prepared the sketch map and index and seized the Alamats and re aided the statements of the witnesses under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He arrested four accused and tried to arrest the-rest of the accused. Finding prima fade case against six accused persons he submitted charge sheet on 30.08.2000 under Sections 302/34/114 of the Penal Code. The accused are Md. Shamim, Md. Arif, Md. Bakuar Rahman, A. Latif, Md. Kamal and Md. Dukhu Miah. Since the prima jade charge could not be proved against the rest accused during investigation he prayed for acquittal of them. This witness identified the sketch map and index and his signatures thereon as Exhibits-3, 3/1 and 4, 4/1 respectively. He seized this electric torch light, a Lungi and part of a blood stained shirt and prepared seizure list. This witness identified the seizure list and his signature thereon as Exhibits-2, 2/3 respectively and also identified the seized Aiamats which were marked as Exhibits-I, II, III. This witness also indentified the Ejahar form and the signature of the then Officer-in-charge Ershadul Kabir Chowdhury as Exhibits-5, 5/1, 5/2 respectively. 

 33. During cross-examination he stated that he recorded the statements of eleven witnesses. He did not visit the place of occurrence personally. He did not hold trial upon assessment of the evidence of witnesses. He denied the suggestion that the witnesses deposed falsely. 

 37. Now let us turn to the evidence, which is available on the record to ascertain the guilt of the convict-appellant Md. Shamim. At this juncture it is worthy to scan the evidence adduced by the prosecution. P.W. 1 stated in his deposition that he was 1½’’ k.m. away at the time of commission of offence and hearing about the incident he rushed to the spot and found the victim in an, injured condition and at that time on his query he came to know from the victim about the names of accused persons who attacked the victim. The victim told him that accused Bakuar pushed him from behind at the behest of accused Latif while accused Shamim chopped him and others beat him. But none of the P.Ws. in their testimony deposed asserting the fact that P.W.1 was present while the victim made the dying declaration. 

 39. P.W. 1 stated in his deposition that while making dying declaration by the victim, Samad, Siddiq, Sattar, Ilahi,  Mianur, Atiar Molla, Nazrul, Aminur,  Rafiqul and many other local people were  present at the place of occurrence. P.W.1 also stated his deposition that one Mofiz from Rova Office came near to the microbus while the victim was being lifted to the microbus for sending the victim to hospital. P.W.10 the Investigation Officer of the case stated in his cross- examination that one Harunur Rashid brought the water from his house to pour on the head of the victim. From the record it appears that although the prosecution examined Samad (P.W3), Aminur (P.W.4) and Siddiq (P.W.8), but did not produce Sattar, Ilahi, Mijanur, Atiar Molla, Nazrul, Rafiqul and Mofiz as witnesses, which impeaches the credibility of the prosecution case. The prosecution claims that on the day of occurrence the victim was returning to his home after sipping tea from the tea stall of Dipu but said Dipu and other tea stall owners beside the shop of Dipu had not been made witnesses in the case. Again, P.W.1 in his cross- examination could not state the name of person from whom he learnt about the information of attack on the victim. In the aforesaid backdrop the court may draw an inference under Section 114(g) of the Evidence Act, 1872 that had those witnesses been examined they would not support the prosecution case. 

 "It is to be observed that a dying declaration, although a piece of substantive evidence has always beef: viewed with some degree of caution as the matter is no liable, to cross-examination. A dying declaration, however, otherwise stands on the same footing as any other piece of evidence and has to be judged in the light of surrounding circumstances and common human experience. When there is a record of such statement of the deceased the court has to satisfy itself, in the first place, as to the genuineness of the same keeping in view all the evidence and circumstances in which the statement of the deceased was said to have been recorded. 

 42. In the said case their Lordships finally held that-  '....... Having considered all aspects of the case we have found it impossible to hold that alleged dying declaration, the only piece of evidence against the appellant in this case was free from reasonable doubt. That being so he is entitled to the benefit of that doubt." 

 (v) Where the dying declaration is suspicious, it should not be acted upon without corroborative evidence. 

 45. Thus, if a dying declaration is made voluntarily and is found to be genuine and is free from all reasonable doubt keeping in view all the evidence on record it is legal to convict the accused. But in the present case, it has already been found that P.Ws.1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 8 are interested witnesses and the alleged dying declaration made orally in presence of those interested witnesses cannot be salt-to be relied on. More so, P.W.9, the doctor performing autopsy of the deceased stated in his cross-examination that the death of the victim took place instantly after receiving the injuries from which it is logically deduced that the victim was not in a fit condition to make dying declaration. In view of the foregoing discussion, we find that the alleged dying declaration of the victim is not found to be genuine and as such the conviction of the accused Md. Shamim on the basis of the said dying declaration is not tenable in the eye of law. 

 47. Due to the above stated facts, in our opinion, the conclusion reached by the Courts below was not correct. On the basis of such scanty evidence, the Courts below should not have passed the order of conviction in respect of accused Md. Shamim. The trial Court as well as the High Court Division committed illegality misreading the evidence in so far as it relates to the accused Md. Shamim. For The reasons stated hereinabove, we are of the view that the judgment and order convicting the convict-appellant Md. Shamim is not justified and, therefore, this Criminal Appeal is liable to be allowed.  48. Hence it is ordered that the Criminal Appeal No.48 of 2021 preferred by the convict-appellant Md. Shamim is allowed and he is acquitted from the charge levelled against him and his conviction and sentence is set aside. Let him be set at liberty forthwith if not wanted in connection with any other case.
